+# Words, unit edits and bounded shortest paths
+
+## Abstract
+
+Actual binary-word tree geometry
+
+A word is a finite list of Boolean letters in its physical order. APPEND adds one letter at the right end; POP removes exactly that last letter. A path is an actual finite sequence of these edits. Its length counts every edit, and Within requires the initial, intermediate and terminal words all to satisfy the given height bound.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Actual binary words).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.Word`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.Word` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Word is the type List Bool, including the empty word and every finite physical bit sequence.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Longest common initial word).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.lcp`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.lcp` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The function compares the first letters, retains equal letters and stops at the first difference or at an empty word.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Actual unit operations).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.Step`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.Step` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The two constructors relate w to w followed by one Boolean letter, and that extended word back to w. No other transition has unit cost.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Actual edit sequences).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.Path`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.Path` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+An empty sequence stays at its word. A nonempty sequence consists of one actual Step followed by another actual sequence with the matching endpoint.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (Charged path length).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.length`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.length` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The empty sequence has length zero; each actual edit adds one.
+
+**Definition 1.6 (All intermediate heights).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.Within`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.Within` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every path p and natural height L, Within(p,L) requires every word in the sequence, including both endpoints, to have length at most L.
+
+**Definition 1.7 (Common-prefix distance).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.distance`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.distance` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For any words u and v, distance(u,v) is length(u)+length(v)-2*length(lcp(u,v)), using natural subtraction. The common prefix is no longer than either word.
+
+**Theorem 1.8 (Exact shortest actual POP/APPEND distance).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.shortest_pop_append`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry.shortest_pop_append` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every two actual binary words u and v, lcp(u,v) is a prefix of each and contains every common prefix. Every actual edit path from u to v has length at least distance(u,v). There exists an actual path of exactly that length, all of whose word lengths are at most max(length(u),length(v)). The proof bounds the change in distance under each literal APPEND or POP, then constructs the attaining sequence by popping the suffix of u to the common prefix and appending the suffix of v. Empty words and coincident endpoints are included.
+
+For the finite tree consisting of words of length at most L, endpoints in that tree therefore have a shortest path entirely inside the same tree. This supplies the operation-distance statement in section 39 of Recursive Relational Observation IV. The exact distinct unordered near-pair count IV.113, its finite representation bijection, recorder injection IV.112, bound IV.114 and closed form IV.115 are not established here.
+

+/- GID: D5/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry
+   generality: G
+   mirror-B: D5/B/S3/Combinatorics/Graph/Walks/BinaryWordGeometry
+   mirror-E: none(waiver:no-computational-evidence)
+   anchors: [mathlib/module/Mathlib.Data.List.Infix]
+   utility: none
+   digest: Binary-word edits attain common-prefix distance within endpoint heights. -/
+
+import Mathlib.Data.List.Infix
+import Mathlib.Tactic
+
+/-!
+The longest-common-prefix definition and its prefix proofs are adapted from
+vltanh/lean4-camus, revision f6edae966a69a4153f41ee94f679e16c87d798b4,
+Camus/Defs.lean and Camus/Tree/Geometry.lean (Apache-2.0).
+The complete supplier license is docs/reports/third-party/lean4-camus-LICENSE.txt.
+Retire this supplier slice when the pinned mathlib provides equivalent binary-list
+longest-common-prefix declarations, replacing its uses by those declarations.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+namespace D5.S3.Combinatorics.Graph.Walks.BinaryWordGeometry
+
+abbrev Word := List Bool
+
+/-- The actual longest common initial word. -/
+def lcp : Word → Word → Word
+  | [], _ => []
+  | _ :: _, [] => []
+  | a :: p, b :: q => if a = b then a :: lcp p q else []
+
+private theorem lcp_prefix_left (p q : Word) : lcp p q <+: p := by
+  induction p generalizing q with
+  | nil => simp [lcp]
+  | cons a p ih =>
+    cases q with
+    | nil => simp [lcp]
+    | cons b q =>
+      by_cases h : a = b
+      · simp [lcp, h, ih]
+      · simp [lcp, h]
+
+private theorem lcp_prefix_right (p q : Word) : lcp p q <+: q := by
+  induction p generalizing q with
+  | nil => simp [lcp]
+  | cons a p ih =>
+    cases q with
+    | nil => simp [lcp]
+    | cons b q =>
+      by_cases h : a = b
+      · subst b; simp [lcp, ih]
+      · simp [lcp, h]
+
+private theorem prefix_lcp {x p q : Word} (hp : x <+: p) (hq : x <+: q) :
+    x <+: lcp p q := by
+  induction x generalizing p q with
+  | nil => simp
+  | cons a x ih =>
+    cases p with
+    | nil => have := hp.length_le; simp at this
+    | cons b p =>
+      cases q with
+      | nil => have := hq.length_le; simp at this
+      | cons c q =>
+        obtain ⟨rfl, hp'⟩ := List.cons_prefix_cons.mp hp
+        obtain ⟨rfl, hq'⟩ := List.cons_prefix_cons.mp hq
+        simp [lcp, ih hp' hq']
+
+/-- Unit edits are precisely right-end APPEND and its inverse POP. -/
+inductive Step : Word → Word → Prop
+  | append (w : Word) (b : Bool) : Step w (w ++ [b])
+  | pop (w : Word) (b : Bool) : Step (w ++ [b]) w
+
+/-- An actual finite edit sequence; its length counts every charged edit. -/
+inductive Path : Word → Word → Type
+  | nil (w : Word) : Path w w
+  | cons {u v w : Word} (step : Step u v) (tail : Path v w) : Path u w
+
+/-- Exact charged edit count of the actual sequence. -/
+def Path.length {u v : Word} : Path u v → ℕ
+  | .nil _ => 0
+  | .cons _ tail => tail.length + 1
+
+/-- The height restriction charges every intermediate word, including endpoints. -/
+def Path.Within {u v : Word} : Path u v → ℕ → Prop
+  | .nil w, L => w.length ≤ L
+  | @Path.cons u _ _ _ tail, L => u.length ≤ L ∧ tail.Within L
+
+/-- The tree distance, expressed with ordinary natural subtraction. -/
+def distance (u v : Word) : ℕ := u.length + v.length - 2 * (lcp u v).length
+
+private theorem distance_nil_left (v : Word) : distance [] v = v.length := by
+  simp [distance, lcp]
+
+private theorem distance_nil_right (u : Word) : distance u [] = u.length := by
+  cases u <;> simp [distance, lcp]
+
+private theorem distance_cons (a b : Bool) (u v : Word) :
+    distance (a :: u) (b :: v) =
+      if a = b then distance u v else (a :: u).length + (b :: v).length := by
+  have h₁ := (lcp_prefix_left u v).length_le
+  have h₂ := (lcp_prefix_right u v).length_le
+  by_cases h : a = b <;> simp [distance, lcp, h] <;> omega
+
+private theorem append_lipschitz (u v : Word) (b : Bool) :
+    distance u (v ++ [b]) ≤ distance u v + 1 ∧
+      distance u v ≤ distance u (v ++ [b]) + 1 := by
+  induction u generalizing v with
+  | nil => simp [distance_nil_left]; omega
+  | cons a u ih =>
+    cases v with
+    | nil =>
+      simp only [List.nil_append, distance_nil_right, distance_cons]
+      split_ifs <;> simp [distance_nil_right] <;> omega
+    | cons c v =>
+      simp only [List.cons_append, distance_cons]
+      by_cases h : a = c
+      · simpa [h] using ih v
+      · simp [h]; omega
+
+private theorem distance_self (u : Word) : distance u u = 0 := by
+  induction u with
+  | nil => rfl
+  | cons a u ih => simpa [distance_cons] using ih
+
+private theorem distance_symm (u v : Word) : distance u v = distance v u := by
+  induction u generalizing v with
+  | nil => simp [distance_nil_left, distance_nil_right]
+  | cons a u ih =>
+    cases v with
+    | nil => simp [distance_nil_left, distance_nil_right]
+    | cons b v =>
+      simp only [distance_cons]
+      by_cases h : a = b
+      · simp [h, ih]
+      · simp [h, Ne.symm h, Nat.add_comm]
+
+/-- Every actual update sequence costs at least the endpoint tree distance. -/
+private theorem path_lower_bound {u v : Word} (p : Path u v) :
+    distance u v ≤ p.length := by
+  induction p with
+  | nil w => simp [distance_self, Path.length]
+  | @cons u z v step tail ih =>
+    have h : distance u v ≤ distance z v + 1 := by
+      cases step with
+      | append base bit =>
+        rw [distance_symm u v, distance_symm (u ++ [bit]) v]
+        exact (append_lipschitz v u bit).2
+      | pop base bit =>
+        rw [distance_symm (z ++ [bit]) v, distance_symm z v]
+        exact (append_lipschitz v z bit).1
+    simp only [Path.length]
+    omega
+
+private def Path.join {u v w : Word} (p : Path u v) (q : Path v w) : Path u w :=
+  match p with
+  | .nil _ => q
+  | .cons step tail => .cons step (tail.join q)
+
+private theorem Path.join_length {u v w : Word} (p : Path u v) (q : Path v w) :
+    (p.join q).length = p.length + q.length := by
+  induction p with
+  | nil => simp [Path.join, Path.length]
+  | cons step tail ih => simp [Path.join, Path.length, ih, Nat.add_right_comm]
+
+private theorem Path.within_mono {u v : Word} {L M : ℕ} (p : Path u v)
+    (h : p.Within L) (hLM : L ≤ M) : p.Within M := by
+  induction p with
+  | nil => exact h.trans hLM
+  | cons step tail ih => exact ⟨h.1.trans hLM, ih h.2⟩
+
+private theorem Path.join_within {u v w : Word} {L : ℕ} (p : Path u v)
+    (q : Path v w) (hp : p.Within L) (hq : q.Within L) :
+    (p.join q).Within L := by
+  induction p with
+  | nil => exact hq
+  | cons step tail ih => exact ⟨hp.1, ih q hp.2 hq⟩
+
+private theorem Path.start_within {u v : Word} {L : ℕ} (p : Path u v)
+    (hp : p.Within L) : u.length ≤ L := by
+  cases p with
+  | nil => exact hp
+  | cons => exact hp.1
+
+private theorem Step.reverse {u v : Word} (s : Step u v) : Step v u := by
+  cases s with
+  | append base bit => exact .pop _ bit
+  | pop base bit => exact .append _ bit
+
+private def Path.reverse {u v : Word} (p : Path u v) : Path v u :=
+  match p with
+  | .nil w => .nil w
+  | @Path.cons u _ _ step tail => tail.reverse.join (.cons step.reverse (.nil u))
+
+private theorem Path.reverse_length {u v : Word} (p : Path u v) :
+    p.reverse.length = p.length := by
+  induction p with
+  | nil => rfl
+  | cons step tail ih => simp [Path.reverse, Path.join_length, Path.length, ih]
+
+private theorem Path.reverse_within {u v : Word} {L : ℕ} (p : Path u v)
+    (hp : p.Within L) : p.reverse.Within L := by
+  induction p with
+  | nil => exact hp
+  | @cons u v w step tail ih =>
+    exact Path.join_within _ _ (ih hp.2) ⟨Path.start_within tail hp.2, hp.1⟩
+
+private theorem append_path (w s : Word) :
+    ∃ p : Path w (w ++ s), p.length = s.length ∧ p.Within (w.length + s.length) := by
+  induction s generalizing w with
+  | nil =>
+    rw [List.append_nil]
+    simp only [List.length_nil, Nat.add_zero]
+    exact ⟨.nil w, rfl, Nat.le_refl _⟩
+  | cons b s ih =>
+    obtain ⟨p, hlen, hp⟩ := ih (w ++ [b])
+    have result : ∃ q : Path w ((w ++ [b]) ++ s),
+        q.length = (b :: s).length ∧ q.Within (w.length + (b :: s).length) := by
+      refine ⟨Path.cons (.append w b) p, ?_, ?_⟩
+      · simpa [Path.length] using hlen
+      · constructor
+        · simp
+        · simpa [List.length_append, Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_left_comm] using hp
+    rw [List.append_assoc, List.singleton_append] at result
+    exact result
+
+/-- The longest common prefix is certified from the words themselves. Every actual
+POP/APPEND path has at least the displayed distance, and an actual attaining path
+keeps every intermediate word within the larger endpoint length. -/
+theorem shortest_pop_append (u v : Word) :
+    (lcp u v <+: u ∧ lcp u v <+: v ∧
+      ∀ w : Word, w <+: u → w <+: v → w <+: lcp u v) ∧
+    (∀ p : Path u v, distance u v ≤ p.length) ∧
+    ∃ p : Path u v, p.length = distance u v ∧ p.Within (max u.length v.length) := by
+  refine ⟨⟨lcp_prefix_left u v, lcp_prefix_right u v,
+    fun _ hp hq => prefix_lcp hp hq⟩, fun p => path_lower_bound p, ?_⟩
+  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := lcp_prefix_left u v
+  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := lcp_prefix_right u v
+  obtain ⟨p, hplen, hp⟩ := append_path (lcp u v) s
+  obtain ⟨q, hqlen, hq⟩ := append_path (lcp u v) t
+  have hu : (lcp u v).length + s.length = u.length := by rw [← List.length_append, hs]
+  have hv : (lcp u v).length + t.length = v.length := by rw [← List.length_append, ht]
+  have hd : s.length + t.length = distance u v := by unfold distance; omega
+  have hp' : p.Within (max u.length v.length) := p.within_mono hp (by omega)
+  have hq' : q.Within (max u.length v.length) := q.within_mono hq (by omega)
+  have result : ∃ r : Path ((lcp u v) ++ s) ((lcp u v) ++ t),
+      r.length = distance u v ∧ r.Within (max u.length v.length) := by
+    refine ⟨p.reverse.join q, ?_, p.reverse.join_within q (p.reverse_within hp') hq'⟩
+    rw [Path.join_length, Path.reverse_length, hplen, hqlen, hd]
+  rw [hs, ht] at result
+  exact result
+
+#print axioms shortest_pop_append
+
+end D5.S3.Combinatorics.Graph.Walks.BinaryWordGeometry

+**Definition 39.1 (the physical pair count).** Use the causal record
+contract of Definition 34.1. Thus $k\ge1$ is fixed before the inputs,
+$K_0$ is any fixed finite word, every label occurs once in an arbitrary
+order with an arbitrary bit, the settled public input is the exact current
+set $A$, and the only persistent private record is the visible whole word
+$K$. POP and APPEND each cost one, every edit and every intermediate word is
+charged, and separately paid scratch is cleared at each logical cut. For a
+terminal assignment $x\in\{0,1\}^k$, let $R_x$ contain **all** reachable
+terminal words. These fibres may be history-dependent, have many words, and
+be disconnected. Put
+
+$$
+T_L=\{w\in\{0,1\}^{*}:|w|\le L\},\qquad
+\delta(u,v)=|u|+|v|-2|\operatorname{lcp}(u,v)|,
+$$
+
+and, for integers $L,D\ge0$,
+
+$$
+P(L,D)=\#\bigl\{\{u,v\}\subseteq T_L:u\ne v,
+\ \delta(u,v)\le2D\bigr\}.
+\tag{IV.111}
+$$
+
+The metric $\delta$ is the shortest POP/APPEND distance, so every actual
+update path is at least its endpoint distance.
+

+**Theorem 39.4 (prepared native current-term consequence).** Apply the
+contract of Definition 30.1 to the known-alpha, beta-left recorder and use
+the prepared family of Proposition 37.1. Its explicit marker is
+
+$$
+C=\langle\beta,\alpha\rangle,\qquad
+M=\langle\langle C,\alpha\rangle,\alpha\rangle
+=\langle\langle\langle\beta,\alpha\rangle,\alpha\rangle,\alpha\rangle,
+$$
+

+**Definition 39.1 (the physical pair count).** Use the causal record
+contract of Definition 34.1. Thus $k\ge1$ is fixed before the inputs,
+$K_0$ is any fixed finite word, every label occurs once in an arbitrary
+order with an arbitrary bit, the settled public input is the exact current
+set $A$, and the only persistent private record is the visible whole word

+charged, and separately paid scratch is cleared at each logical cut. For a
+terminal assignment $x\in\{0,1\}^k$, let $R_x$ contain **all** reachable

+be disconnected. Put
+

+T_L=\{w\in\{0,1\}^{*}:|w|\le L\},\qquad
+\delta(u,v)=|u|+|v|-2|\operatorname{lcp}(u,v)|,
+$$

+
+$$
+P(L,D)=\#\bigl\{\{u,v\}\subseteq T_L:u\ne v,
+\ \delta(u,v)\le2D\bigr\}.

+**Corollary 39.3 (near-minimal memory and the $D=1$ boundary).** Exact
+terminal decoding gives
+
+$$
+2^k\le|T_L|=2^{L+1}-1,\qquad L\ge k.
+\tag{IV.116}
+$$
+
+Combining (IV.112) with (IV.114) gives the integer necessity
+
+$$
+D\ge
+\left\lceil\log_2\left(1+\frac{k\,2^{k-L}}{10}\right)\right\rceil.
+\tag{IV.117}
+$$
+
+Consequently, for any fixed integer additive allowance $c\ge0$, the regime
+$L\le k+c$ forces
+
+$$
+D\ge\left\lceil\log_2\left(1+\frac{k}{10\,2^c}\right)\right\rceil,
+$$
+
+so the worst logical update is logarithmic in $k$ at fixed additive peak
+redundancy. These are necessary bounds; they provide no matching coding
+construction and do not rule out constant $D$ when an unrestricted linear
+peak is available.
+
+For $D\le1$, the concatenation of the $k$ update paths puts every terminal
+word within distance $k$ of the same $K_0$. A radius-$k$ ball in the binary
+word tree is contained isometrically in a radius-$k$ ball of the infinite
+trivalent tree. That ball has $3\,2^k-2$ vertices and $3\,2^k-3$ edges;
+its $3\,2^{k-1}-2$ internal vertices have degree three. A distance-two
+pair has a unique midpoint, so the number of distance-one-or-two pairs is
+
+$$
+(3\,2^k-3)+3(3\,2^{k-1}-2)=15\,2^{k-1}-9.
+$$
+
+Thus (IV.112) excludes $D\le1$ for every $k\ge15$ with arbitrary fixed
+$K_0$. If $K_0=\varepsilon$, all terminal words lie in $T_k$, and (IV.115)
+gives $P(k,1)=5\,2^k-7$; hence the same obstruction excludes $D\le1$ for
+$k\ge10$. These are sufficient exclusions, not sharp thresholds, and they
+make no claim that every fixed $D>1$ is impossible.
+
+The parameters $k=L=10,D=1$ separate static capacity from update capacity:
+$T_{10}$ has $2047$ words for $1024$ assignments, but (IV.112) asks for
+$5120$ distinct physical pairs while $P(10,1)=5113$. The model itself is
+inhabited at peak $L=k$: initialize $K_0=0^k$, let public $A$ select the
+labelled positions in $K$, and rebuild the required tail in paid scratch;
+this has exact current decoding, peak $k$, and at most $2k$ paid edits per
+arbitrary-order update. With a fixed known arrival order, appending each
+new bit gives the separate comparison $L=k,D=1$. Neither comparison is a
+construction for the unrestricted logarithmic-update target.

+**Theorem 39.2 (edge-specific pair-capacity obstruction).** Every
+admissible causal recorder with finite peak $L$ and worst logical update bill
+$D$ satisfies
+
+$$
+ k2^{k-1}\le P(L,D),
+\tag{IV.112}
+$$
+
+and, for every $L,D\ge0$,
+
+$$
+P(L,D)=
+\sum_{t=1}^{L}2^{L-t}
+\left(\sum_{d=1}^{\min(2D,t)}2^d
++\sum_{\substack{1\le i,j\le t\\i+j\le2D}}2^{i+j-2}\right).
+\tag{IV.113}
+$$
+
+Moreover,
+
+$$
+P(L,D)\le5\,2^L(2^D-1),
+\tag{IV.114}
+$$
+
+for all $L,D\ge0$, and the closed form
+
+$$
+P(L,D)=5\,2^L(2^D-1)-(D+1)2^{2D}+1
+\tag{IV.115}
+$$
+
+holds whenever $L\ge2D-1$ (in particular, for every $L\ge0$ when
+$D=0$).
+
+**Proof.** Let $e=\{x,y\}$ be a Boolean-cube edge whose differing label is
+$j$. Run all other labels first in one fixed order, with their common bits.
+The two runs have the same initial word and the same first $k-1$ inputs, so
+causality gives the same word $z_e$ immediately before the last insertion.
+If internal choices are allowed, choose one allowed outcome of this common
+prefix and use that same outcome for the two completions; the all-outcomes
+contract makes both completions admissible. Let $u_e\in R_x$ and
+$v_e\in R_y$ be the two terminal outputs. Each last
+update has at most $D$ actual edits, hence
+$\delta(u_e,v_e)\le\delta(u_e,z_e)+\delta(z_e,v_e)\le2D$.
+Exact terminal decoding makes $u_e\ne v_e$. If two cube edges selected the
+same unordered pair of words, decoding that pair would give the same
+unordered pair of assignments, and hence the same cube edge. Thus
+$e\mapsto\{u_e,v_e\}$ is injective. This proves (IV.112). The argument uses
+no global choice of one representative per assignment and no connectedness
+of any $R_x$; an assignment can use different representatives on its
+incident edges.
+
+For the count, assign a distinct word pair to its unique lowest common
+ancestor $w$. If $w$ has depth $L-t$, there are $2^{L-t}$ choices for it.
+If one endpoint is $w$ and the other is $d$ edges below, there are $2^d$
+choices for $1\le d\le\min(2D,t)$. Otherwise the endpoints lie in opposite
+child subtrees at distances $i,j\ge1$ from $w$, with $i,j\le t$ and
+$i+j\le2D$; there are $2^{i-1}2^{j-1}=2^{i+j-2}$ choices. The left/right
+roles count each unordered pair once. Summing over $t$ proves (IV.113),
+including the empty sum for $L=0$ or $D=0$.
+
+For $D=0$ every count is zero. Assume $D\ge1$. Divide (IV.113) by
+$2^L$ and extend the nonnegative sum to all $t\ge1$. An ancestor term of
+depth $d$ contributes
+$2^d\sum_{t=d}^{\infty}2^{-t}=2$, so these terms contribute $4D$. A
+cross-branch pair $(i,j)$ contributes
+$2^{i+j-2}\sum_{t=\max(i,j)}^{\infty}2^{-t}=2^{\min(i,j)-1}$. For
+$m=\min(i,j)$ there is one diagonal pair and $2(2D-2m)$ off-diagonal
+pairs. Therefore
+
+$$
+4D+\sum_{m=1}^{D}(4D-4m+1)2^{m-1}=5(2^D-1),
+$$
+
+which gives (IV.114). When $t\ge2D$, the inner bracket in (IV.113) is
+constant and equals
+
+$$
+\sum_{d=1}^{2D}2^d+\sum_{s=2}^{2D}(s-1)2^{s-2}
+=(D+1)2^{2D}-1.
+$$
+
+If $L\ge2D-1$, every omitted term in the infinite geometric sum has
+$t\ge2D$. Its normalized tail is therefore
+$2^{-L}((D+1)2^{2D}-1)$, and subtracting it from
+$2^{-L}5\,2^L(2^D-1)$ proves (IV.115). For $D=0$, both sides are zero for
+all $L$. $\square$
+

+import LeanInformationAuditInterface.Contract.Registration
+import D5.S3.Combinatorics.Graph.Walks.BinaryWordGeometry
+import Reg.Support.DependentFamily
+
+/-! A full-source audit with the lower-bound distance observation varied. -/
+
+open LeanInformationAudit
+open _root_.D5.S3.ConceptDynamics.InformationEscape.DependentFamily
+open _root_.D5.S3.Combinatorics.Graph.Walks.BinaryWordGeometry
+
+namespace Reg.D5.S3.Combinatorics.Graph.Walks.BinaryWordGeometry
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+abbrev signature : Signature where
+  Params := Word
+  State _ := Word
+  Role := Unit
+  finiteRole := inferInstance
+  nonemptyRole := inferInstance
+  Output _ _ := ℕ
+  Anchor := Empty
+  finiteAnchor := inferInstance
+
+def actual : Realization signature :=
+  realize signature (fun _ u v => distance u v) (fun e => nomatch e)
+
+def rejected : Realization signature :=
+  realize signature (fun _ _ _ => 1) (fun e => nomatch e)
+
+abbrev arena : Arena where
+  signature := signature
+  Law r := ∀ u v : Word,
+    (lcp u v <+: u ∧ lcp u v <+: v ∧
+      ∀ w : Word, w <+: u → w <+: v → w <+: lcp u v) ∧
+    (∀ p : Path u v, r.readout () u v ≤ p.length) ∧
+    ∃ p : Path u v, p.length = distance u v ∧ p.Within (max u.length v.length)
+
+private theorem rejected_law : ¬ arena.Law rejected := by
+  intro h
+  have bad := (h [] []).2.1 (.nil [])
+  change 1 ≤ 0 at bad
+  exact (by decide : ¬ (1 : ℕ) ≤ 0) bad
+
+def source_registration : Registration arena (type_of% shortest_pop_append) where
+  actual := actual
+  bridge := Iff.rfl
+  variation := ⟨shortest_pop_append, rejected, rejected_law⟩
+  sensitivity := by
+    constructor
+    · intro i
+      refine ⟨rejected, ?_, rfl, rejected_law⟩
+      intro j h
+      exact (h (Subsingleton.elim _ _)).elim
+    · intro e
+      exact nomatch e
+  dependence := by
+    intro i
+    refine ⟨[], [], [true], ?_⟩
+    change (0 : ℕ) ≠ 1
+    decide
+
+def registration : LeanInformationAudit.Contract.Registration.{_,_,_,0,0,0,_,_,_,_,_,0}
+    (@shortest_pop_append) (Realization signature) Unit Unit := {
+  unitName := `Reg.D5.S3.Combinatorics.Graph.Walks.BinaryWordGeometry.unit
+  realizationName := `Reg.D5.S3.Combinatorics.Graph.Walks.BinaryWordGeometry.source_registration
+  realizationSource := none
+  generated := false
+  arena := .source ⟨arena⟩
+  objectArena := .source ⟨arena⟩
+  catalog := Lean.Name.anonymous
+  localNames := false
+  realization := .source arena ⟨source_registration⟩
+  correspondence := { stage := .evidence, objectStage := .evidence }
+  bundleNonempty := .absent
+  readout := some (realize signature (fun _ u v => distance u v) (fun e => nomatch e))
+  variation := .absent
+  sensitivity := .absent
+  partialSensitivity := none
+  escapeFrom := none
+  sourceSelection := some {
+    owner := `D5.S3.Combinatorics.Graph.Walks.BinaryWordGeometry
+    definition := none
+    coordinates := #[0]
+    readouts := #[
+      { path := #["body", "body", "arg", "fn", "arg", "body", "fn", "arg"]
+        stateBinder := 1
+        functionOperand := false
+        stateOperand := none
+        booleanPredicate := false }] }
+  continuation := .unknown
+  familyRecord := none
+  options := #[] }
+
+#print axioms source_registration
+#print axioms registration
+
+end Reg.D5.S3.Combinatorics.Graph.Walks.BinaryWordGeometry
